raw_response:
I've been farming this land for 30 years, since I was 21. My father taught me everything — I never went to school, can't read, but I know this 6 mu like the back of my hand. Wheat in winter, maize in summer, every year. It's tight work, especially that week between wheat harvest and maize planting, but me and my wife manage. We have four mouths to feed, so every yuan I spend has to come back.

This year, I'll do about the same as last year. Last year the wheat was decent — I got about 420 jin per mu, which is fine. The maize was a bit less because of the dry spell in July, maybe 480 jin per mu. I won't change much. Change is risky.

**For the wheat:** I'll plant around October 8th, same as always. I buy the seed from the shop in town — it's that improved variety most people use, not the fanciest hybrid but reliable. Costs me about 45 yuan per mu. Before planting I spread about 80 jin of that compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu as base, and then at jointing time in spring I topdress with about 30 jin of urea. That's roughly 12-13 kg of nitrogen per mu total, I reckon — the shopkeeper told me once, but I just know it as two big bags for the 6 mu. I irrigate three times: once after planting if it's dry, once at jointing when the wheat is hungry, and once at grain filling. Pumping water is expensive now, about 35 yuan each time for my 6 mu, but you can't skip it. I spray herbicide once in early spring — the weeds will choke you otherwise. I'll harvest around June 10th. Me and my wife do most of the work, but I might hire Old Wang's combine for one day, costs about 60 yuan per mu.

**For the maize:** Plant right after wheat harvest, probably June 12th or 13th. Three, maybe four days to get it in the ground — I work from dawn to dark those days. I use hybrid maize seed, about 3.5 kg per mu, costs around 55 yuan. At planting I put down another 60 jin per mu of compound fertilizer. Then at big trumpet stage — around late July — I topdress with 25 jin of urea per mu. Total nitrogen is maybe 11 kg per mu. I irrigate twice if it's dry: once right after planting to help it sprout, and once at flowering if the rain doesn't come. Some years I only irrigate once, but last July was dry so I'll plan for two. I spray herbicide once and maybe insecticide if I see worms — last year I didn't need it, but I'll watch. Harvest late September, probably by hand because the combine for maize costs too much for just 6 mu.

**Money:** I'm careful. Total cash I can spend on inputs this year is about 2,000 yuan, and I need to stay under that. Fertilizer prices went up a bit, so I'm thinking about whether I can cut back on the maize topdress, but no — last time I skimped on maize fertilizer I lost almost 100 jin per mu. Better to borrow a little from my brother than risk that. Water and fertilizer are the two things you can't cheat on.

My son is working in the factory now, so it's just me and my wife in the fields most days. My mother is old and stays home. We can handle the 6 mu without hiring much labor — maybe 3 days total for hired help at harvest time.
